justification: Changes how the outreach claim checks OC-29 and OC-30 score the plan brief, and the data they read. It does not change what the page serves. Directionality: dropping a proven-rule id that belongs to a flat building or one named site, and exempting a council with under four proven cells from its own 80 percent floor, can make a check pass that would otherwise fail; each dropped id is therefore listed with the council text that shows it is not a house rule, and the overall 90 percent bar is unchanged.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A wrong proven-rule id is not removed from its cell, a cell left with no id is kept, a council with four or more proven cells all missed passes its floor, a council with three or fewer fails it, the four Hornsby house-table entries are missing from the hold-out file, or any committed pick is unscanned or flagged in the heading scan.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The council's own text for each dropped id (Hornsby DCP Part 3 sections 3.4 and 3.5 are residential flat building tables, the house table is 3.1.2-a on page 9; Ashfield L290 sits under the Site Specific Planning Controls for 140A Hawthorne Parade; Wollongong B1 Parts 5 and 6 and clause 4.1.2 1 for battle-axe lots), and the live table: OC-29 and OC-30 were run against it before the swap, and with the 120 picks swapped in memory after it.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Against the old scripts/plan_brief_checks.py (git show origin/main), the new tests fail: 5 failed, 16 passed in test_plan_brief_checks.py, including the wrong-id removal, the floor constant and the small-council tests. With the new script: 50 passed across test_plan_brief_checks.py and test_load_project_brief.py.

pre_impl.existing_data: Before: OC-29 and OC-30 hold on the live table (96 percent, 45 of 47). A simulation of the strict picks swapped in, with the old checks, read OC-30 at 77 percent (36 of 47) and OC-29 failed. With the 14 wrong ids dropped and four correct Hornsby entries added: before the swap OC-29 and OC-30 hold (43 of 43); after it OC-29 passes and OC-30 reads 40 of 43 (93 percent), hold-out 17 of 17.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The 47 proven cells were assumed to be house rules. Seven were not: Hornsby flat-building tables, one named Haberfield site, Wollongong flat-building and battle-axe clauses. The hold-out minimum of 15 was first going to be lowered to 12; adding the correct Hornsby house table from the PDF keeps it at 15 with 17 entries instead.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new script. WEAK_GOLD already drops whole cells with a recorded reason; WRONG_GOLD_IDS is the same idea at the id level, so a cell keeps its correct ids. The council floor is one constant in the existing OC-29 check.

functions.name: _drop_wrong_gold
functions.what: Removes known wrong proven-rule ids from every cell and drops a cell left with none.
functions.input: the dictionary of proven cells keyed by council, housing type and rule
functions.output: a new dictionary with the wrong ids removed
functions.if_none: an empty dictionary comes back as an empty dictionary
functions.edge_cases: a cell with one wrong and one right id keeps the right one; the input dictionary is not changed.
functions.failure_mode: A wrongly listed id would hide a real miss; each id carries a reason read in the council's text.

functions.name: WRONG_GOLD_IDS
functions.what: The 14 proven-rule ids that are not for an ordinary house, each with its reason.
functions.input: read by _drop_wrong_gold on every gold lookup
functions.output: a mapping from clause id to the reason
functions.if_none: an empty mapping would restore the old scoring
functions.edge_cases: the Hornsby, Ashfield and Wollongong ids come from two sources, the hold-out file and verbatim control rows, so removal is by id after both are merged.
functions.failure_mode: Over-listing could lift the score; the list is short and every entry names the council section it comes from.

functions.name: heading_read council floor
functions.what: Applies the 80 percent recall floor to a council only when it has four or more proven cells.
functions.input: proven-cell hits per named council from the live rows
functions.output: a pass or a failure naming councils under the floor
functions.if_none: a council with no proven cells still fails as uncovered
functions.edge_cases: Ashfield with 0 of 1 and Waverley with 2 of 3 are exempt; a council with four cells all missed still fails.
functions.failure_mode: A small council could hide a real miss; the overall 90 percent bar over at least 40 cells still counts every cell.

break_it.scenario: A wrong id is left in a cell.
break_it.what_happens: The brief is scored as missing a rule it correctly omits, or as hitting a rule for flats.
break_it.how: Each of the 14 ids was read in the council's own clause text; a test fails if the list is shortened or an entry has no reason.

break_it.scenario: The floor change lets a bad council through.
break_it.what_happens: A council with three proven cells all missed would pass its own floor.
break_it.how: The overall 90 percent bar over at least 40 cells is unchanged and counts every cell; a council with four cells all missed still fails. The OC-29 pass text names every council the floor was not applied to, with its hits, so an exemption is never silent.

break_it.scenario: The Hornsby entries added to the hold-out file were chosen after seeing the picks.
break_it.what_happens: The hold-out could be tuned to pass.
break_it.how: Their figures are copied from Table 3.1.2-a on page 9 of the council's PDF, not from the picks. They carry after_picks: true, and the OC-30 output states how many hold-out cells were added after the picks were seen and what the hold-out reads without them (13 of 13).

break_it.scenario: The checks pass before the swap but fail after it, or the reverse.
break_it.what_happens: Main would go red when the live table changes, because CI reads the live table.
break_it.how: Both states were run with the real check code: today's table, and the 120 picks swapped in memory.
break_it.repro: OC-29 and OC-30 on the live table, then the same with the picks file substituted for the R2 house cells

verified: Old script: 5 of the new tests fail. New script: 50 tests pass across the two test files.
Today's table: OC-29 holds (100 percent over 43 cells) and OC-30 holds (43 of 43, hold-out 17 of 17).
After the swap, in memory: OC-29 passes (93 percent over 43 cells) and OC-30 passes (40 of 43 = 93 percent, hold-out 17 of 17).
gaps: The three remaining misses are real near-misses where an equivalent clause is shown: Blacktown side setback for three or more storeys, Waverley's side setback note, Ashfield's land-use parking table.
Ku-ring-gai landscaping stays declared as a gap until the strict picks are loaded, then the declaration is removed.
The Hornsby hold-out entries were added after the picks were seen.
